# Jubilees Chapter 47 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Moses' birth and early life; Mastema's first attempt on Moses

---

**47:1** In the seventh year of the seventh week of the forty-seventh jubilee, the LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, and the angel of the presence spoke to Moses according to the word of the LORD.

**47:2** A new king arose over Egypt who oppressed the children of Israel. He said: "Let us kill their males, lest they multiply and wage war against us."

**47:3** Pharaoh commanded that every male child born to the sons of Israel be cast into the river and drowned.

**47:4** A man of the tribe of Levi went and took as wife a daughter of Levi. She conceived and bore a son. She saw that he was beautiful and hid him for three months.

**47:5** When she could no longer hide him, she made for him a basket of bulrushes, plastered inside and out with pitch, placed the child in it, and set it among the reeds at the river's bank.

**47:6** His sister stood at a distance to see what would happen to him.

**47:7** The daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe in the river, and her attendants walked along the riverbank. She saw the basket among the reeds and sent her maidservant to fetch it.

**47:8** She opened it and saw the child, and the child was crying. She had compassion on him and said: "This is one of the Hebrew children."

**47:9** His sister came up and said to Pharaoh's daughter: "Shall I go and find you a nurse from the Hebrew women to nurse the child for you?" Pharaoh's daughter said: "Go." The girl went and called the child's own mother.

**47:10** Pharaoh's daughter said to her: "Take this child and nurse him for me, and I will pay your wages." The woman took the child and nursed him.

**47:11** When the child grew older, she brought him to Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, saying: "Because I drew him out of the water."

**47:12** In those days Moses grew up in Pharaoh's house and was greatly loved by Pharaoh. He was taught all the wisdom of the Egyptians.

**47:13** Mastema came and sought to kill Moses. But the LORD said to him: "His time has not yet come." And Mastema withdrew from before him.

---

*LOGOS notes: The birth narrative follows Exodus 2:1-10 closely. The Mastema episode (v.13) is a Jubilees addition connecting this to the later confrontation in ch.48, where Mastema assists the Egyptian magicians against Moses. The framing verse (v.1) places the entire narrative as spoken from Sinai through the angel of presence.*
